vendors.name: CreativeX
vendors.notes: No public pricing page. Closest direct competitor (enterprise creative quality/governance).

vendors.name: Smartly.io
vendors.notes: No pricing link in nav. Verify attribute-level creative analysis before scoring creative-outcome-link LOUD (taxonomy revision #5).

vendors.name: Celtra
vendors.notes: Pricing page exists: contact-sales, bespoke, dimensions = impressions/video starts/volume.

vendors.name: Pencil (Brandtech)
vendors.notes: Transparent pricing: Core $14/mo, Growth $55/mo, Pro custom; metered on generations/month. Category-residency watch: drifting toward 'AI operating system'.

vendors.name: Alison.ai
vendors.notes: Tier structure public (Essential/Pro+/Enterprise) but no dollar amounts.

vendors.name: DAIVID
vendors.notes: SCRAPE-HOSTILE: JS SPA returning only <title> to plain fetches; old /what-we-do/ 404s. Needs headless rendering or scores false-ABSENT on everything. Classify as UNOBSERVABLE, not ABSENT, where capture is empty.

vendors.name: Dragonfly AI
vendors.notes: Tiers Light/Scaling/Enterprise, dimension 'Test up to 200 assets', no dollar amounts.

vendors.name: Motion
vendors.notes: JS-heavy homepage; /llm-info is a machine-readable mirror (copy written FOR scrapers — surface-rule question: does llm-info count as LOUD?). Transparent spend-tiered pricing: Starter $250/mo up to $50k/mo ad spend.

vendors.name: Segwise
vendors.notes: Fills the mobile/UA cell Replai vacated. Pricing page JS-rendered; 7-day free trial, no credit card.

claims.capability: Pre-flight creative scoring: a numeric/graded quality score computed on an asset BEFORE it runs, used as a go/no-go or budget gate
claims.definition: LOUD if hero/product-page promises scoring assets pre-launch (e.g. 'checking all new content before it goes live'); QUIET if scoring exists only inside docs/case studies; ABSENT if all analytics are post-hoc on live ads.

claims.capability: Predicting in-market performance (CTR/ROAS/conversion) of an ad before any impressions are served
claims.definition: Distinct from quality scoring: vendor claims to forecast OUTCOMES, not adherence. LOUD if 'predict performance before launch' appears on hero/product page; QUIET if framed as 'insights inform future ads'; ABSENT if no forward-looking claim.

claims.capability: Biometric/panel-trained AI predicting human visual attention or salience on creative
claims.definition: LOUD if attention prediction is the hero claim (e.g. 'patented biological algorithm'); QUIET if attention is one metric among many; ABSENT if no human-response modeling claimed.

claims.capability: Predicting emotional response to creative (discrete emotion taxonomy, e.g. DAIVID 39)
claims.definition: LOUD if named emotion framework on homepage; QUIET if 'emotions' listed inside a feature bullet; ABSENT otherwise.

claims.capability: In-flight creative optimization: recommendations on LIVE campaigns (kill/scale/iterate) while spend is running
claims.definition: LOUD if 'mid-flight optimization' or real-time creative recommendations on hero/product page; QUIET if only periodic reporting on live ads; ABSENT if analysis is strictly pre/post campaign.

claims.capability: Vendor platform ACTIONS the optimization itself (pauses/launches/budget-shifts via ad-platform APIs)
claims.definition: LOUD only if automated execution is claimed ('launch, manage, update campaigns auto-magically'); recommendations alone do NOT qualify. ABSENT for read-only analytics vendors.

claims.capability: Automated brand-guideline/suitability checking (logo, safe zones, brand-early, audio mention) on every ad
claims.definition: LOUD if compliance/governance is a hero or named-product claim; QUIET if guideline checks appear only as scoring sub-metrics; ABSENT if no brand-rules concept.

claims.capability: Enterprise governance across markets/agencies: one creative standard enforced across regions and production partners
claims.definition: LOUD if 'global scale' / multi-market / agency-partner enforcement is hero-level; QUIET if multi-market shows only in case studies; ABSENT if single-team product.

claims.capability: Computer-vision/AI auto-tagging of creative elements (hooks, CTAs, people, audio, pacing) with zero manual setup
claims.definition: LOUD if auto-tagging is a named feature on hero/product page; QUIET if tagging exists but is manual/taxonomy-setup-required; ABSENT if no element-level decomposition.

claims.capability: Tying specific creative attributes to business KPIs (ROAS, CTR, sales) — the core 'creative data' claim. Requires attribute/element granularity, not just media reporting.
claims.definition: LOUD if hero claims creative-to-outcome causality at attribute level; QUIET if correlation reporting buried in features; ABSENT if creative and media metrics never joined.

claims.capability: AI generation of new ad creative explicitly grounded in the vendor's own performance/creative data (insight-to-asset loop)
claims.definition: LOUD if generate-from-insights is hero-level; QUIET if generation is a beta/add-on; ABSENT if vendor is analytics-only. Generic genAI without the data loop does NOT count.

claims.capability: Governed enterprise genAI: model aggregation + IP indemnification + SOC2 + brand-safe agents for creative production
claims.definition: LOUD if governance of AI usage (not of brand assets) is the headline; QUIET if security page only; ABSENT if no genAI controls story.

claims.capability: Named native integrations with Meta + TikTok + YouTube (minimum trio) for creative-level data pull
claims.definition: LOUD if platforms named on homepage/product hero; QUIET if list lives only in docs/FAQ/integration pages; ABSENT if platform-agnostic uploads only.

claims.capability: CTV/online-video-specific creative analytics or activation (beyond paid social)
claims.definition: LOUD if CTV named in hero/suite copy; QUIET if CTV only in a solutions footnote; ABSENT if social-only.

claims.capability: Competitor creative intelligence: analyzing competitors' ads or category benchmarks
claims.definition: LOUD if a named competitive product exists in nav; QUIET if 'benchmarks' mentioned without competitor data source; ABSENT otherwise.

claims.capability: Creative fatigue prediction/detection before performance decay burns budget
claims.definition: LOUD if fatigue is a named feature; QUIET if only a metric in dashboards; ABSENT otherwise.

claims.capability: Creative scores/attributes exposed via API/data feed into customer BI, CDP, or media stack
claims.definition: LOUD if API is a named nav product; QUIET if API mentioned in docs only; ABSENT if data exits via CSV/dashboard only.

claims.capability: Creative effectiveness as an input variable to marketing mix models / econometrics
claims.definition: LOUD if MMM integration is productized and on-site; QUIET if it exists only as a partnership press release; ABSENT otherwise.

claims.capability: Agency-specific offering: multi-client management, client reporting, agency packaging
claims.definition: LOUD if dedicated /agencies solution page linked from nav; QUIET if agencies named only in customer logos; ABSENT if single-advertiser product.

claims.capability: Measuring diversity/inclusive representation in ad creative as a tracked metric
claims.definition: LOUD if named nav product with dedicated page; QUIET if a sub-metric; ABSENT otherwise.

claims.capability: Named agentic-AI creative strategist: an agent that answers strategy questions and produces briefs/next-creative recommendations
claims.definition: LOUD if a named agent product exists ('AI Strategist', 'AI Studio'); QUIET if 'ask AI follow-ups' chat affordance only; ABSENT if no agent framing.

claims.capability: Self-serve entry: published dollar pricing and/or free trial without sales contact
claims.definition: LOUD if dollar amounts or 'start free, no credit card' on a public pricing page; QUIET if tier names published without prices; ABSENT if pricing page 404s or demo-gate only.

claims.capability: Pricing metered on monthly ad spend analyzed (not seats, not impressions served)
claims.definition: LOUD if spend thresholds printed; QUIET if 'pricing scales with your spend' without numbers; ABSENT if seats/asset/impression metered or undisclosed.

claims.capability: Vendor-supplied human creative/production services bundled with the platform
claims.definition: LOUD if services in primary nav; QUIET if services exist but unlinked from product story; ABSENT if pure software.

claims.capability: Local-market adaptation: regional/market teams adapt or version global creative for their market (transcreation, localization, language/format versioning) inside the platform
claims.definition: LOUD if localization/transcreation/market-versioning is hero or named-product level ('adapt global campaigns for every market'); QUIET if localization appears only as a feature bullet or case-study capability; ABSENT if no multi-market adaptation story. Distinct from multimarket-governance: governance ENFORCES a standard from the center; this claim EMPOWERS the edge to produce. SPLITTER: enterprise buyer, distributed operation.

claims.capability: Guardrailed edge self-serve: non-central teams (regional, brand, field) create and launch creative themselves within centrally-set brand guardrails — 'freedom within a framework'
claims.definition: LOUD if edge-team self-serve within central rules is hero/named-product ('let every team create on-brand'); QUIET if templates/locked-elements/permissions exist as buried features; ABSENT if creation happens only centrally or by the vendor. Requires BOTH delegation and guardrails — pure template tooling without governance language does not count. SPLITTER: enterprise buyer, distributed operation.

claims.capability: Multi-brand portfolio operations: a parent organization managing many brands/business units in one account — separate workspaces, permissions, cross-brand rollups
claims.definition: LOUD if portfolio/multi-brand management is hero or named-product ('every brand in your portfolio'); QUIET if multi-workspace/multi-brand support appears only in feature lists or pricing tiers; ABSENT if single-brand product. Multi-app support for ONE team (e.g. a UA team's game portfolio) is at most QUIET — the claim is about a brand-parent org structure. SPLITTER: enterprise parent purchase, delegated operation.

claims.capability: Centralized creative ops for performance: one central creative-ops/studio function serving many performance pods — shared tag taxonomies, naming conventions, asset libraries, standardized reporting enforced across teams and accounts
claims.definition: LOUD if a central-ops/standardization story is hero/named-product ('one source of truth for every team's creative'); QUIET if shared libraries, tag taxonomies, or cross-account standardization appear as buried features; ABSENT if single-team product. Distinct from agency-multiclient-workflow: that serves an AGENCY managing external clients; this serves an in-house central function serving internal pods. SPLITTER: performance buyer, centralized operation.

config.surfaceRule: LOUD = hero copy OR top-level-nav named product with dedicated page; QUIET = present on any indexed page below that (docs, FAQ, llm-info, blog, sub-metrics); ABSENT = nowhere observed; UNOBSERVABLE = capture empty/JS-walled (never score ABSENT from a failed capture). Open question: machine-targeted pages (Motion /llm-info) currently score QUIET-leaning-LOUD.

axes.label: Buyer altitude
axes.rubric: Who the claim is addressed to: a global brand/marketing organization buying standards and measurement (-1) vs a single performance/growth team buying campaign outcomes (+1). Scores derived from each claim's icp label; validated against independent audience-vocabulary derivation (spearman 0.80) and pricing transparency (0.73) on run-1.

axes.label: Operating model
axes.rubric: Who adopts and enforces the claimed capability: a central brand/marketing-ops function setting standards across business units and markets — the global Coca-Cola CMO (-1) — vs a single team or regional unit buying for its own campaigns — the LATAM regional Dasani team (+1). PROPOSAL: scores are first-pass labels pending Ryan's review; agency-multiclient-workflow flagged genuinely ambiguous (centralized across clients, distributed relative to the brand org).

axes.label: Intervention point
axes.rubric: When the claimed capability intervenes relative to media spend: before any impression is served (-1) vs on live campaigns while budget burns (+1). Pricing-structure claims score null (axis does not apply). PROPOSAL: first-pass labels.

axes.label: Value mode
axes.rubric: What the claimed capability does to creative: evaluates, scores, or reports on it (-1) vs produces, adapts, or executes it (+1). Plumbing/pricing claims score null. Discovered as run-1 PC2 (max-variance direction orthogonal to buyer); rubric positions validated against PC2 vendor scores.
